explanation: If the node has a right subtree, return its leftmost node. Otherwise follow parents while coming from a right child; the first ancestor reached from its left child is next in inorder.
timeComplexity: O(h): follow a downward or upward path, not a whole-tree search. Native functions begin at the target, while C#/JavaScript first search the tree to resolve its data identifier.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. C#/JavaScript use a height-sized DFS stack to locate the target; native code begins with the node and needs only a cursor.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/successor_in_tree.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Inorder visits the right subtree immediately after a node, beginning at that subtree’s leftmost node. Without a right subtree, every ancestor reached from a right child has already been visited. The first left-child ascent reaches the first unvisited ancestor, or no successor exists.
walkthrough: For node 9 in [14,6,22,3,9,18,27,null,4], there is no right child. Ascend from 9 to 6 through a right edge, then from 6 to 14 through a left edge. Return node 14. JSON arguments are [tree,nodeData]. Native wrappers resolve the node and call the one-node function; C#/JavaScript receive tree and data.
edgeCases: The callable receives one existing nonnull node with valid parent links.
The last inorder node has no successor and returns null/None.
The wrapper resolves node_idx as a data value, then displays the successor data or −1.
